data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The panel is fundamentally less reliable because 'objectively verifiable' outcomes often emerge from non-linear synthesis that a checklist cannot capture, making the panel's 'reliability' an illusion of high-frequency success on simple cases.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The task is truly additive, where the outcome is a simple sum of discrete verifiable parts.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist includes exhaustive conditional logic (if/then) that replicates the expert's synthesis.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The 'Synthesis Gap': Experts use a high-dimensional mental map to weigh variables non-linearly. A checklist, by definition, is a linear or branching set of discrete checks. In complex verifiable tasks, the 'right' answer depends on the interaction between checklist items (e.g., Item A is only relevant if Item B is False). The panel lacks the synthesis capability to handle these dependencies, making them 'reliably' wrong on complex cases while appearing 'reliably' right on simple ones.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
